original_instruction: Can you run this please locally? https://github.com/xliry/banodoco-wrapped
original_user_context:
# Native user behavior and task phases — v2

The initial request only asks to run the application locally. It does not disclose the optimization work. The host must send the registered optimization follow-up at the first conversational checkpoint, before accepting completion. That follow-up authorizes changes to TopGenerations and ModelTrends. Do not assume that the initial instruction contained it.

After the follow-up, let the agent implement and validate. Ask about mobile/responsive behavior when virtualization is proposed without considering it. Correct animation issues only when observed: it must start from zero on first and later loads, advance through all available data, reveal timeline labels with data, and ease out without premature completion. Suggest inspecting built-in chart animation if it conflicts with custom progression. If the animation finishes in under roughly three seconds, ask to slow it down. New-model labels should be white, remain visible long enough to read, and track their model's segment. Do not invent browser observations or claim to have seen execution that is absent from the records. If browser verification is unavailable, ask for an honest limitation and source-based reasoning.

Prefer concise feedback. Do not repeatedly restate disclosed scope. Answer clarification questions from the registered goals. A persona review preference governs the initial review phase; the explicit registered follow-up authorizes the implementation phase. Accept only when the substantive work and currently disclosed persona requests have been addressed, with remaining verification limitations stated honestly.

required_followups.text: Now please optimize the running application. In TopGenerations, load approximately four rows of videos at a time, load upcoming rows while scrolling, and release off-screen videos; use viewport observation and clean it up. Preserve responsive/mobile behavior. In The Rise & Fall of Models (ModelTrends), start playback when the section enters view. Start from zero and reveal data from the left on the first and subsequent loads; continue through all data rather than stopping early. Use smooth ease-out timing, normalize each nonempty row to a full share, and keep the Y-axis fixed at a full-share range (0–100 percent or 0–1 fractions). Reveal time labels as entries become visible. Show a white model-name label when a model enters, keep it readable, and have it follow the model's segment. Make the necessary code changes and check the production build. Report what you actually verified; do not claim browser results without running them.
